thread:
Alex: Heads up — saw a bunch of 2-minute GPU cold starts during today's traffic spike in eu-west1. CA spun up many T4 spot nodes but pods still queued because GPU init + our model pull is ~90s. Any quick flags/heuristics to avoid these weird fractional packing/coldstart thundering herd issues?

Sanjay: Can you paste the CA flags and a sampled pod describe? also which expander are we using atm?

Alex: Using `--expander=most-pods` and mixed nodegroups: a100-on-demand, t4-spot, t4-on-demand. Pod describe snippet:```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2s (x5 over 1m)  default-scheduler  0/50 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
We see CA choosing many t4-spot nodes but each node gets only 1 GPU-using pod because we have lots of small workloads. Result: lots of nodes partially filled, cost spike, and boot queue because each pod waits for driver + model pull.

Maria: Two angles: (1) expander + binpack heuristics to prefer filling existing GPU nodes, (2) pre-warm / node-init to cut the 90s. For CA try `--expander=binpacking` or enable `--balance-similar-node-groups` to avoid scattering across pools.

Alex: Interesting — we tried binpacking earlier but rolled back due to weird cross-AZ skew. Do you have specific flags to tweak?

Maria: Sure, try these increments:```
--expander=binpacking 
--balance-similar-node-groups=true 
--max-node-provision-time=10m 
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m 
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
```
`max-node-provision-time` lets CA wait a bit longer for nodes to come up before launching more. `utilization-threshold` encourages packing.

Ryan: Also consider `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` only if you know your DS semantics; otherwise CA will avoid draining nodes with local state. And check PDBs — they often block scale-down and force CA to create new nodes instead of consolidating.

InfraBot: Note: there was a provisioning event at 2026-03-17T09:12Z for nodepool t4-spot-eu-west1b (provision latency 85s).

Jen: Related gotcha — kube-scheduler spreading and our PodTopologySpread for GPUs can cause one-pod-per-node. Double-check `topologySpreadConstraints` and any anti-affinity. If you want densification, relax those or add `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` rules.

Lucas: For short term mitigation we run a tiny DaemonSet on GPU pools that preloads driver+weights and keeps a tiny warm process so the kernel modules are ready. Example init job:```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: gpu-warmup
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
      containers:
      - name: warmup
        image: our-registry/gpu-warmup:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/warm-driver && sleep 3600"]
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 0
```
That cut cold-init from 90s to ~10s on a test pool. Caveat: heavier image pulls increase t4 spot churn cost.

Sanjay: Another trick: tag nodegroups with `node.k8s.io/instance-type: t4` and use CA's `--node-group-auto-discovery` label filters + custom expander plugin (we've got an internal small script) to prefer nodegroups with existing GPU utilization.

Alex: Thanks all. I'll flip to binpacking + balance-similar flags in staging, add the warmup DS in a canary t4 pool, and monitor CPU/GPU packing. Will report back with metrics (packing ratio, median provisioning time, cost delta). :thumbsup:

Maria: If you hit a fallback where CA keeps scaling because of Pod disruption budgets, ping me — we instrumented eviction traces that helped us tune `--scale-down-unneeded-time` safely.

Alex: Great — assigning self to roll this out now. If it helps later I can paste flame graphs for scheduler latency.
